root_cause.cause: The extent of MDQ-PR-028 was not searched in the exercises, and no mechanical check finds a test that starts threads without waiting for them to start.
root_cause.escape: The test passes on an idle machine; CI's jobs run tests with fewer parallel jobs than CPUs, and the stress run does not select exercise tests.

reports.title: The release bundle could not name the compiler of a build configured through a toolchain file
reports.found: 2026-11-04, CI run of ci.yml on 83f2e4c, job reproducible-build: tools/release_bundle.py make stopped with KeyError: 'CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER'
reports.description: Chapter 32 moved the choice of compiler from a cache variable of the presets to toolchain files. A toolchain file sets CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER as a variable, so a fresh build tree's CMakeCache.txt has no entry for it, and release_bundle.py, which reads the compiler's version for the bundle's toolchain record from the cache, failed. tools/test_report.py read the same entry and would have written '?' in the system test report. The job's error path also lost the build logs: 'tail -30' with several files is refused by tail.

evaluation.rationale: A release tool failed loudly before any release; the product is unchanged.

resolution.change: Both tools fall back to the value that CMake records in the build tree (CMakeFiles/<version>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake) when the cache has no entry; repro_check.sh uses 'tail -n 30'.
resolution.verification: Both tools name /usr/bin/g++ for a fresh hardened build tree; tools/repro_check.sh on the fixed commit; CI's reproducible-build job.

whys: The bundle step found no CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER in the cache.
Since the toolchain files, CMake no longer caches the compiler.
The change was tested in build trees configured before it, whose caches still held the entry from the earlier presets, so every local tool run passed.
No local check configures a fresh build tree; CI's jobs do, and found it.
root_cause.cause: A change to how the build is configured was verified only in build trees that predated it.
root_cause.escape: Local runs reused build directories whose caches kept the old entry.

reports.title: ADR 0027 did not list its options as the ADR format requires

reports.title: Two packages pinned in the analysis lock file had published vulnerabilities that nothing reported
reports.found: 2026-11-04, SOUP review for release 0.7.0: the Python Package Index lists 55 advisory records against pillow 12.3.0 (fixed in 13.0.0) and one against Pygments 2.17.2 (fixed in 2.20.0)

The SOUP review covered the items it named, and the lock file was recorded as one row of section 2.

root_cause.escape: The lock file was added in Chapter 31 with a license and version review, without a vulnerability lookup.

reports.title: Exercise 10.4's speed test also asked for an absolute rate with no margin
reports.found: 2026-11-04, release checks of 0.7.0, part 1, on 1572784: ch10/e4_fast_sorter/solution/FastSorter.FastEnough failed in the hardened preset with 29.2 M singles/s against 30 M
reports.description: FastSorter.FastEnough checks two things: the solution is at least 1.9 times the baseline (with the margin of MDQ-PR-040) and it exceeds 30 M singles/s inside the energy window. The second is an absolute rate of the machine at the moment of the run. The reference solution reaches about 50 M alone in the hardened build and 42 to 49 M with six busy processes, but fell to 29.2 M while the release checks ran the other tests beside it. The CAPA's margin table listed only the ratio.

evaluation.rationale: A test of an exercise; MiniDAQ's code and tests are unchanged.

resolution.change: The absolute rate is checked only when EX_MIN_SINGLES_PER_S is set, on a quiet machine the reader has measured; the ratio stays the default check. The test still records both rates. README and Chapter 10's exercise text say so; CAPA-0001's table row names both criteria.
resolution.verification: The test passes in the release and hardened builds alone and under load; with EX_MIN_SINGLES_PER_S=30e6 on the quiet machine it passes at about 50 M.

whys: The test failed at 29.2 M against 30 M while the machine was busy.
An absolute rate depends on the machine and its load; a ratio of two sorters measured interleaved does not.
The margin review of 0.5.0 (MDQ-PR-040) changed and tabled the ratio and did not see that the same test had a second criterion.
The table has one row per test and one criterion per row.
root_cause.cause: A speed test with two criteria was reviewed against the margin rule for one of them.
root_cause.escape: The rate held on the quiet machine and in CI's runners; only the release checks run the hardened build's tests with other heavy tests beside them.

reports.title: The release checks built the starters with Unix Makefiles, under which Exercise 32.3's tests skip
reports.found: 2026-11-04, release checks of 0.7.0, part 1: 'passes every test: ch32/e3_rebuild/starter'
reports.description: Exercise 32.3's tests ask Ninja which files a change rebuilds (a dry run) and skip with another generator. tools/release_checks.sh configures build/starters without a generator, so CMake chose Unix Makefiles, the three tests skipped and the starter passed. The check of the starters did its job and reported it.

evaluation.rationale: A release check of the exercises; MiniDAQ is unchanged.

resolution.change: release_checks.sh configures build/starters with -G Ninja, as the presets do.
resolution.verification: With Ninja, Exercise 32.3's starter fails one test and its solution passes; the starter check of the release checks run again.

The tests need Ninja and the starter build used CMake's default generator.
Exercise 32.3 was verified in the exercise build tree, configured by a preset with Ninja, not in the release checks' own build.

reports.title: The test cmake.consumer asked for recon 0.7 and failed when VERSION moved to 0.8.0-dev
reports.found: 2026-11-04, full ctest after VERSION moved to 0.8.0-dev: 'with requested version "0.7" ... version: 0.8.0'
reports.description: recon/tests/consumer/CMakeLists.txt named a fixed version in find_package(recon 0.7). The package's version file uses SameMinorVersion, so a build of 0.8.0 refuses a request for 0.7, as Chapter 32 says it should. The package was right; the test was written for one version.

evaluation.rationale: A test of the build's installed package; no shipped program changed.

resolution.verification: cmake.consumer passes with VERSION 0.8.0-dev; the whole ctest passes.

reports.title: minidaq_sim reported as recorded the singles it had simulated past the end of the run
reports.found: 2026-11-04, Chapter 33's end-to-end run: minidaq_sim said 445,867 recorded singles for a run of which minidaq_send, from the same seed, sent 445,866
reports.description: DetectorSimulator::generate_until stops at the first single at or after the end and keeps it for the next call; its statistics count every single it has simulated, that one included. minidaq_sim printed those statistics as 'recorded singles', while its list mode, its sorter report and its count rates used only the singles before the end. Over three seeds the difference was one single each time.

evaluation.rationale: A line of the simulator's printed summary, a development tool; no coincidence, list-mode file, sinogram or count rate changed, and no measurement in the book quotes the line.

resolution.change: minidaq_sim prints the number of singles it uses as 'recorded singles' and, when there are any, the singles simulated past the end on their own line.
resolution.verification: tools/e2e.py and the test system.e2e: the singles the reference records equal the singles minidaq_send sends from the same seed; the whole ctest passes.

whys: The printed count and the count of the singles used differed by the singles past the end.
The line printed the simulator's statistics, which count every single simulated, not the singles returned.
Nothing compared that line with another stage's count until a chain put two programs side by side.
root_cause.cause: A summary printed a counter of one quantity under the name of another.
root_cause.escape: No test reads minidaq_sim's printed summary; the simulator's tests check the singles it returns. The end-to-end accounting of Chapter 33 is the first check that compares counts across programs.

reports.title: system.e2e failed in every CI build job: the daily QC step could not import SciPy
reports.found: 2026-11-04, the CI runs of Chapter 33's commits: system.e2e failed in the six build-test jobs (FileNotFoundError on qc/report.json) and passed on the development machine
reports.description: tools/e2e.py runs the daily QC of Chapter 31 (python -m minidaq_analysis) on the point-source acquisition. The CI build-test jobs install NumPy but not SciPy or Matplotlib, which the analysis package needs, so the QC process stopped at its imports without writing a report, and e2e.py read the missing report and raised an exception instead of failing a check. The development machine has both packages, so the release checks passed there.

evaluation.rationale: A verification tool and the CI environment; no product code, no shipped program and no recorded measurement changed. The test failed loudly, so no result was taken from it.

resolution.change: The build-test jobs of ci.yml install python3-scipy and python3-matplotlib (the versions Ubuntu 24.04 ships meet analysis/pyproject.toml's minimums). tools/e2e.py records a QC run that writes no report as a failed check whose equation carries the QC tool's exit status and last error line.
resolution.verification: system.e2e passes in the six CI build-test jobs; daily_qc on a run record the QC tool rejects gives the failed check 'QC: the daily QC report passes' with the tool's message, and no exception.

whys: The QC process wrote no report in CI.
It could not import SciPy, which the CI build jobs do not install.

The analysis package's own tests skip in those jobs when their tools are missing, and the end-to-end test was the first build-job test to run the package; it was written and run where the packages were present.
root_cause.cause: A test that runs a second program assumed that program's dependencies were in the environment, and treated its missing output as impossible.
root_cause.escape: The release checks run on the development machine, which has every package; a new system test was not run in a CI-like environment before it was pushed. The CI failure was seen on the next look at the runs, before the release.

reports.title: fuzz_calibration aborted on a valid table: its oracle remembered a NaN that a later edit had overwritten
reports.found: 2026-11-04, the CAPA-0001 check of release 0.8.0: CI job fuzz-smoke on the Part VII review's commit (1eb2b89) failed with fuzz.calibration; the input was in the job's log and reproduced on main
reports.description: In edit mode the target applies up to 64 edits to a valid calibration table and expects the reader to accept exactly when the final table is valid. It decided 'not finite' with a flag set when any edit wrote a NaN or an infinity, so an input that wrote a NaN to a coefficient and later overwrote it with a finite value expected a rejection; the reader accepted the finite table, correctly, and the target aborted. The failure was on the review branch's run and went unread: the branch was merged locally after the main thread's own CI was green.

evaluation.rationale: A defect in a test's oracle; the calibration reader behaved as specified on the input (it accepted a table of finite values with a right CRC), and no product code changed.

resolution.change: The target decides whether the table holds a value that is not finite from the values it ends with. The input is a seed, corpus/calibration/regress-nan-overwritten, and a row of fuzz/README.md's findings.
resolution.verification: fuzz_calibration on the input exits 0; the CI job fuzz-smoke and the release fuzzing of 0.8.0 run the target from the corpus that holds it.

whys: The target expected a rejection for a valid table.
Its flag recorded the history of the edits, not the state of the table that the reader saw.
A failed CI run on a review branch was not read before the branch was merged; only the main branch's runs were checked.
root_cause.cause: A test oracle computed from the operations instead of from the result they produced, and a red run on a branch that nobody read.
root_cause.escape: The release 0.7.0 fuzzing did not reach the input; the review branch's run did, and the merge looked only at the runs on main. The CAPA-0001 check of every failed run of the period found it.

reports.title: The release checks' performance gate discarded its build's output, so a failed build left no reason
reports.found: 2026-11-04, release checks part 3 for 0.8.0 on d262ff0: 'FAIL performance regression gate' with an empty perf-suite.txt, no perf-current.json and no perf-gate.txt
reports.description: tools/release_checks.sh sends the output of 'cmake --preset release' and 'cmake --build' in the gate step to /dev/null, so when that step failed, within a second of starting, nothing said why. Run again by hand with the output kept, the same commands configured and built without error, and the suite ran.

evaluation.rationale: The release checks' evidence, not the product; the failure was visible (the check failed) and the gate was run again in full before any verdict was taken.

resolution.change: The configure and build output of the gate step goes to perf-suite.txt with the suite's own output.
resolution.verification: bash -n tools/release_checks.sh; the test tools.release_checks; the next release run of part 3 keeps the build's output in perf-suite.txt.

whys: The gate step failed with no output.
Its build commands wrote to /dev/null, chosen to keep the log short.
Every other step keeps its output; this one was written when the build was assumed to have been done by an earlier part.
root_cause.cause: A step of the release evidence discarded the output that explains its own failure.
root_cause.escape: The step had never failed before, so the missing output had never been needed.

reports.title: The end-to-end sorter equation left out the out-of-order singles, and a damaged short run passed with any check failed
reports.found: 2026-11-04, the review of Part VIII: tools/e2e.py's sorter partition against Chapter 10's and Exercise 33.1's
reports.description: tools/e2e.py checked 'energy rejected + alone + 2 x pair windows + in multiples = singles in'. The sorter's partition has a fifth term, the out-of-order singles, which the server reports in its status. A run with an out-of-order single would have failed the check as a lost count, and an out-of-order counter off by one failed no check. The test of the equations built its counters without out_of_order, so it could not see the gap. Separately, the short damaged-link test of system.e2e asserted four named checks and that the exit status matched the result, so a damaged run with any other check failed (the sorter's balance, the sink, the files) still passed it.

evaluation.rationale: A verification tool, not the product. Every measured run had no out-of-order single (the readout reorders packets before the sorter), so no verdict was wrong; the gap would have shown as a false failure, not a false pass, of the partition check.

resolution.change: The partition includes out_of_order; the test's consistent counters include it, so the off-by-one test now covers it; the damaged-link test requires every check of both acquisitions to pass and the exit status 0.
resolution.verification: tools/test_e2e.py with the programs (system.e2e): passes; with the old equation the consistent-counter tests fail. The damaged run with --loss and --duplicate 0.005, seeds 1, 2 and 33, passes every check.

whys: A counter the sorter reports was in no equation.
The equation was written from the counters seen in a clean run's status, where out_of_order is always 0.
The off-by-one test changed only the counters in its own fixture, written from the same equation.
root_cause.cause: The equations and the test that checks them were derived from the same list, so they shared its omission.
root_cause.escape: The off-by-one test iterates over its fixture, not over the counters the server reports.

reports.title: The acceptance tool matched a commit by any prefix, so --commit with one or two characters made every evidence fresh

The tool compared prefixes without a minimum length.
The exercise of the same chapter was written with the rule after the tool, and the tool was not revisited.

reports.title: The trailer parser followed git 2.43, and CI's git 2.56 does not take the scheme of a URL for a trailer key

The development machine and the runners have different git versions, and only the runners had the newer one.

reports.title: The end-to-end latency's 99th percentile exceeds 10 ms in about one interval in a hundred, with no change to the code
reports.found: 2026-11-08, release checks of 1.0.0, part 3: ACC-04 failed with 178 of 180 intervals within 10 ms
reports.description: The soak of release 1.0.0 had two 10 s intervals whose 99th percentile was above 10 ms (32.2 ms at 350 s, 23.2 ms at 880 s); the programs of release 0.9.0 on the same machine the same evening had two as well (up to 38.8 ms), and releases 0.8.0 and 0.9.0 had 15 and 1. No source of the product changed since 0.8.0. The steal time the soak records (CR-0025) was 0.5% to 0.9% in those intervals, like the others; averaged over 10 s and four CPUs it cannot show a stall of 30 ms, so the machine is neither shown nor ruled out as the cause. The finer measure exists since the review of 2.0.0 (tools/soak.py, one-second steal and run-queue wait per server thread); its first 30-minute run (measurements/review-2.0.0/) had no interval above 10 ms, a median largest wait of 31 ms per second and up to 204 ms with a 99th percentile of 3 ms (correlation 0.13), so waits of that size alone do not explain a peak; the cause is still to be found in a run that has one. A 100-minute soak for release 2.0.1 (measurements/mdq-pr-064/) had none either: 600 intervals, p99 at most 8.16 ms, correlation 0.14. On 2026-11-21 an unpinned 100-minute soak had 2 of 600 intervals above 10 ms (18.09 and 13.57 ms) whose largest waits (24 and 26 ms) and steal were typical of the run (median wait 26.3 ms, correlation 0.04); a pinned one (mdq-pair and mdq-write sharing a CPU) had 9 of 600, up to 98 ms, with mdq-write's wait 125 ms per second in every interval alike. MiniDAQ's own scheduling is not shown as the cause and pinning makes it worse; at 2.0.x, 2 of 1,740 intervals have had a peak, 0.11%, at most 0.36% at 95% confidence (measurements/mdq-pr-064/).

evaluation.rationale: No single was lost or arrived after the sorter's window in those intervals (the soak counts no loss), the latency is not a risk control of a hazard, and the delay before a fault is noticed is MDQ-PR-006, which does not depend on it.

reports.decision: Release 1.0.0 with a recorded deviation for ACC-04. Find the cause with a finer measure of the machine during the soak (the steal and run-queue time of the pipeline's threads per second, from /proc/self/task/*/schedstat) before the latency limit is judged again. Decided again on 2026-11-22 by the software lead (the author), in writing in the project, on the soaks of measurements/mdq-pr-064/: SRS-PERF-022 is met (2 of 1,740 intervals at 2.0.x, at most 0.36% at 95%, against 1%), and ACC-04 is judged on a 100-minute soak, six of 600 intervals allowed (CR-0035). No setting for the threads' CPU affinity: pinning made the peaks worse.

resolution.change: CR-0035: the release soak lasts 100 minutes, so ACC-04's share of 99% is judged over 600 intervals (six may be above 10 ms) instead of 180 (one); acceptance.json, release_checks.sh, the SRS, SDP and STP. The programs do not change.
resolution.verification: measurements/mdq-pr-064/: 1,740 intervals at 2.0.x with 2 peaks, and the pinned and unpinned soaks with the per-second measure; tools.acceptance: test_the_latency_holds_in_99_percent_of_the_intervals (six of 600 pass, seven fail) and the 30-minute soak refused by ACC-03; the release soak of 2.1.0.

whys: Releases 0.8.0, 0.9.0 and 1.0.0 failed ACC-04 with no change to the code.
The peaks are rare (about one interval in a thousand) and come from outside what the guest's run-queue and steal counters see; neither marks them, and pinning the threads makes them worse.
A criterion of 99% judged on 180 intervals allows one peak, so a compliant release failed it up to 14% of the time: the sample was too small for the rate the requirement allows.
root_cause.cause: ACC-04's soak was too short to judge a share of 99%: one interval in 180, where peaks from the machine occur at about 0.1%.
root_cause.escape: CR-0025 set the share without computing how often a compliant release would fail it at the soak's length; the Clopper-Pearson computation of Exercise 33.4 would have shown it.

reports.title: Chapters 2, 3 and 8 quote measured numbers with no file under measurements/

The reruns agree with every printed conclusion (the latency ladder, SoA 2.3 times faster from DRAM, the arena about 12% faster, the memory-order and batching gaps, the pipeline slowest at batches of 4,096); single values differ by VM noise, most for DRAM latency and false sharing, as the READMEs say.
