reports.title: The decoder's fuzz target still counted a time marker as a single or an invalid crystal
reports.found: 2026-11-15, CI on main (fuzz-smoke) after CR-0026
reports.description: CR-0026 taught the stream decoder to count a time marker (crystal 32767, energy code 2047) in DecodeStats::markers instead of invalid_crystal. The fuzz target fuzz_decoder checks that every word is accounted for as words == decoded + invalid_crystal; it was not updated, so the first input with an all-ones word aborted it within a second. The decoder is right: the property was stale.

evaluation.rationale: The defect is in a test; the decoder's counting of markers is what CR-0026 specifies and its unit tests verify. No release carries it: the release checks of 1.3.0 had not reached the fuzzing.

resolution.change: fuzz_decoder accounts for markers (words == decoded + invalid crystal + markers), checks the count of markers against the words, and checks that the chunked decode gives the same count and the same latest marker as the decode in one call. The all-ones input is kept as the seed seed_marker. Chapter 7's text names the three ways a word is accounted for. Committing that seed showed a second defect: the pre-commit hook read the staged diff as UTF-8 text and crashed on the raw bytes; it now decodes with replacement, a test commits a file of raw bytes, and .gitattributes marks the fuzz corpus as binary.
resolution.verification: The old target aborts on seed_marker and the new one passes it; the new target ran 90 s (3.4 million inputs) from the seed corpus without a finding, and the fuzz CTest runs pass.

whys: The fuzz target's property names the decoder's counters, and a new counter changed what the property must add up.
CR-0026's impact analysis listed the decoder's unit tests but not the fuzz target, and the fuzz targets run only in CI's fuzz-smoke job and the release checks, not in the local test run.
root_cause.cause: A change to the decoder's counters was not traced to every test that states a property over them.
root_cause.escape: The local ctest run before the commit excludes the fuzz label (it needs the fuzz preset); CI's fuzz-smoke job found it on the first push.

reports.title: The stream decoder is 16% slower than in release 1.2.0
reports.found: 2026-11-15, the release checks of 1.3.0 (performance regression gate, part 3)
reports.description: CR-0026 added the time marker to StreamDecoder::decode as a test before the crystal-ID check, so every single paid a comparison of the crystal and the energy code before the one comparison it paid before. The regression gate against book-v1.2.0, both built and run interleaved on the reference machine, measured BM_DecodePacked/65536 at a speed of 0.842 (p = 0.0001) and failed the release checks.

evaluation.rationale: The decoder stays far inside its budget (about 10% of a core at 30 million singles per second before the change); no single was lost and SRS-PERF-020 and SRS-PERF-021 passed. The gate is there to stop a cost that no functional test sees.

resolution.change: The decoder's loop works on local copies of the unwrapper and the crystal count, which no store through the output span can alias, and compares the crystal ID once; a word at or above the crystal count (a marker or an invalid ID) goes to not_a_single, a cold function off the loop. The constructor takes a crystal count above 32767 as 32767, so the marker's crystal is never a single. The behavior is unchanged for every word when the crystal count is below 32768, as for every scanner MiniDAQ knows (18,432 crystals); with a larger count, crystal 32767 at another energy than the marker's is now an invalid crystal, where it was a single (StreamDecoder.KeepsTheLatestOfSeveralMarkersAndNeverTakesTheMarkerForASingle; noted by the independent review of 1.3.0). Chapter 24 says what the gate found and why the order of the tests matters; Chapter 2 says where the branch for rare IDs is.
resolution.verification: tools/perf_ab.sh against book-v1.2.0, five interleaved rounds on the reference machine: BM_DecodePacked/65536 at a speed of 0.973, within the gate's 5%, every gated benchmark ok (it was 0.842 before the fix). Reordering the tests alone measured about 0.86: the loop reloaded the decoder's members for every word. The unit tests of the decoder and the time markers pass, and fuzz_decoder ran 60 s without a finding.

whys: The marker test was written in the order of the specification, a marker before a single, not in the order of frequency.
CR-0026's verification ran the functional tests and the fuzz targets; the benchmarks and the gate run only in the release checks and in CI's perf workflow, which nobody read before the release.
root_cause.cause: A new branch was put on the hot path of every word without a measurement before the commit.
root_cause.escape: The perf workflow, which compares each push to main with its parent on a GitHub runner, failed on CR-0026's commit (run 43721772090) and was not read; the next push compared with an already slower parent and passed. The release checks' gate, which compares with the previous release, caught it as designed. Since then the author checks every workflow of a push, not only ci.

reports.title: verify-run ends with an exception on a signed record whose digest has a field of the wrong type
reports.found: 2026-11-15, the coverage review of release 1.3.0

evaluation.rationale: The record must first pass the Ed25519 check with a key the site installed, so only a trusted signer can make such a record, and the server writes the fields with the right types. The tool then stops with an uncaught nlohmann::json type_error instead of a refusal: no run is believed that should not be, and the failure is visible.

reports.decision: Release 1.3.0 with it: the defect needs a malformed record signed with a trusted key, and the release checks ran on the code as it is. Fix in milestone 2.0.0-dev: verify_signed_run checks that sha256 is a string and bytes an unsigned number before it reads them, with a test that signs such a record (the test of malformed signed records added in this review shows the pattern). Fixed earlier than planned, by the independent review of 1.3.0, so that 2.0.0-dev starts without it.
reports.description: verify_signed_run reads each digest with d.value("bytes", 0) and d.value("sha256", ""). nlohmann::json::value throws type_error.302 when the field exists with another type (checked: a sha256 that is a number throws "type must be string, but is number"); d.value("file", "") throws the same way. verify-run also accepted a file named "." or ".." with the size and digest of no bytes: on Linux a directory opens and reads as empty. The independent review of 1.3.0 found the same defect in the analysis package: verify_run let json.JSONDecodeError, AttributeError and TypeError through for a signed record that is not JSON, is not an object or names a file with a number. CAPA-0003 asked for checked accessors on untrusted input; the record is verified before it is parsed, so it was treated as trusted, but a signed record is not necessarily a well-formed one.

resolution.change: verify_signed_run checks the type of every field before it reads it: a digest's file and sha256 are strings and bytes an unsigned number, or the record is refused with its reason ("has no digest", "its digest has no size or no SHA-256"). A file name that is empty, "." or ".." is refused like a path, and a listed file that is not a regular file cannot be read. The analysis package's verify_run makes the same checks and turns a signed text that is not JSON into a SignatureError.
resolution.verification: Signing.ASignedRecordThatDoesNotListItsFilesProperlyIsRefused signs, with a trusted key, records with a sha256 that is a number, a size that is a string or negative, no sha256, a digest whose file is a number, the names "", "." and "..", and a directory with the digest of no bytes; it ended with an exception before the change (checked) and passes after it, with the other 411 unit tests of the debug build. analysis/tests/test_signature.py::test_a_malformed_record_signed_by_a_trusted_key_is_refused does the same for the package (it failed with json.JSONDecodeError before the change); ruff and mypy pass.

whys: The record's fields were read with nlohmann::json::value, which throws when the field exists with another type, and in Python with dict.get and the / operator, which raise for a value of another type.
The record is checked with its signature before it is parsed, so the parser treated it as trusted input; a signature says who wrote the record, not that it is well formed.
root_cause.cause: Checked accessors (CAPA-0003) were not used on input that a signature had vouched for.
root_cause.escape: CR-0027's tests changed bytes of signed runs, which the signature check refuses before any field is read; only a test that signs a malformed record reaches the parser. The coverage review of 1.3.0 wrote that test and found the defect after the release checks.

reports.title: The server crashes when a board of the hardware description cannot be opened
reports.found: 2026-11-15, CR-0029, the product build's system test
reports.description: SlowControlHardware::open returns an error before it creates the slow control when a board's bus cannot be opened (an mmio device that does not exist, or since CR-0029 a simulated board in a product build). The half-made adapter is then destroyed, and its destructor called stop() and power_down() on the slow control, which did not exist: minidaq_server --hardware ended with SIGSEGV instead of the message 'hardware: ...'.

evaluation.rationale: It happens only at start-up, before the control API listens and before any bias is set: the server does not start, as it should, but with a crash report instead of the reason. No run is affected.

resolution.change: The destructor stops the slow control and switches the bias off only if the slow control exists.
resolution.verification: HardwareService.ABoardThatCannotBeOpenedIsAnErrorNotACrash opens a description whose mmio device does not exist: it ended with SIGSEGV before the change (checked) and passes after it. system.product's test of simulated boards in the product build, which found the defect, passes.

whys: The destructor assumed the invariant of a fully constructed adapter, but open() destroys a partly built one on its error paths.
No test opened a description whose board fails to open: the mmio tests use the simulated board or a file that exists.
root_cause.cause: An error path of a factory function ran a destructor that relied on the object being complete.
root_cause.escape: The error path of MmioBus::open is reached only with a device that is missing at start-up; the unit tests of the configuration check the description, not its opening, and the system tests of the hardware use simulated boards.

reports.title: The server waits for a passphrase on the terminal when its signing key is encrypted
reports.found: 2026-11-15, review of release 1.3.0
reports.description: SigningKey::load read the key with PEM_read_PrivateKey and no passphrase callback, so OpenSSL's default callback asked for a passphrase on the terminal when the key file was encrypted. A server started by the service manager has no terminal: it waited at start-up, or, without a terminal at all, refused the key as 'not an Ed25519 private key in PEM form', which names the wrong cause.

evaluation.rationale: It happens at start-up, before the control API listens: the server does not start, or names a wrong reason. No run is affected and nothing is signed with a wrong key.

resolution.change: The key is read with a callback that gives no passphrase and notes that one was asked for; an encrypted key is refused with 'is encrypted: the server reads only an unencrypted key, protected by the permissions of its file' and the openssl command that writes one. Chapter 25 says how the key is stored.
resolution.verification: Signing.AnEncryptedKeyIsRefusedWithoutAskingForAPassphrase writes an AES-256 encrypted Ed25519 key and loads it: it failed before the change (checked) and passes after it, with stdin closed so that no prompt can answer.

whys: The key loader passed no callback, and OpenSSL's default for an encrypted PEM is an interactive prompt.
The tests wrote unencrypted keys only.
root_cause.cause: A library default meant for interactive programs was used in a service.
root_cause.escape: Every key the tests and the measurements made was unencrypted; the review of 1.3.0 found it by reading the call.

reports.title: minidaq_update stops with a library exception on a state.json whose version is not a string
reports.found: 2026-11-16, internal audit before release 2.0.0 (CAPA-0005, reading every parser of a file)
reports.description: SlotStore::open checked that state.json's good is a string and that trial is present, then read good_version and trial_version with nlohmann's value(key, ""), which throws when the key is there with another type, and took a trial of any type other than a string for no trial. A state.json changed by a person or by the disk ended minidaq_update with '[json.exception.type_error.302] type must be string, but is number' instead of 'state.json is damaged: a person must look at ...', and a trial of 7 was silently forgotten.

evaluation.rationale: minidaq_update is a one-shot tool whose main reports the exception and exits with an error, so nothing is installed or switched; the message names the library's error rather than the damaged file, and a site would need a person either way (coding standard rule 3.5 allows a one-shot tool this). No run or acquisition is affected.

resolution.change: Every field of state.json is type-checked before it is read: the versions must be strings when present, and the trial a string or null; anything else is 'state.json is damaged'.
resolution.verification: Update.OpenRefusesAStoreItCannotTrust gains three damaged states (a number as good_version, 7 as trial, an array as trial_version): it failed before the change (checked) and passes after it. fuzz_documents, whose seed state-mdq-pr-074 is this input, ended with the exception before the change and runs clean after it.

whys: The state file is written by minidaq_update itself, so its reader was written for the files the writer makes.

Rule 3.4 asks for a fuzz target for each parser of external input; the files of the update store, the hardware description, the token file and the signed run record had none, so nothing fed them a field of another type.
root_cause.cause: Files written by MiniDAQ's own programs or by a site's administrator were not counted as external input, so their parsers had no fuzz target (CAPA-0005).
root_cause.escape: No test or fuzz target changed a field's type in state.json; the unit tests damage the file with whole-document cases.

reports.title: minidaq_listmode sino stops with a library exception when the delayed window in the metadata is not an integer
reports.found: 2026-11-16, internal audit before release 2.0.0 (CAPA-0005, reading every parser of a file)
reports.description: minidaq_listmode sino reads records.delayed_window_ps from the first file's metadata with get<std::int64_t>() after checking only that the key exists. Metadata whose window is a string, or whose records is not an object, ended the tool with '[json.exception.type_error.302] type must be number, but is string' and status 2, instead of the warning it gives when the key is missing and its default window.

evaluation.rationale: minidaq_listmode is a one-shot tool whose main reports the exception and exits with an error; no sinogram is written, so no wrong image can follow. The server always writes the window as an integer, so only a file changed after the run reaches it.

resolution.change: The tool checks that records is an object and the window an integer before reading it; otherwise it warns 'no integer records.delayed_window_ps in the metadata' and uses its default, as for a missing key.
resolution.verification: tools/test_listmode_tools.py (tools.listmode) writes a copy of a run's first file whose window is a string of the same length, with the header CRC made again, and runs sino: it failed with the exception before the change (checked) and passes after it.

whys: The metadata is written by MiniDAQ's own sink, so its reader was written for the files the sink makes.
The list-mode fuzz target checks the reader of the format, not the tool's use of the metadata's fields.
root_cause.cause: Files written by MiniDAQ's own programs were not counted as external input, so the reads of their fields were not checked as rule 3.5 asks (CAPA-0005).
root_cause.escape: No test changed a field's type in the metadata; the tools' tests change bytes of blocks, which the CRCs catch.

reports.title: The QC report stops with a Python traceback when the metadata's scanner or records has a field of another type
reports.found: 2026-11-16, internal audit before release 2.0.0 (CAPA-0005, its preventive action)
reports.description: report.fill read the first file's metadata with meta['scanner'] and meta['records'].get(...) and int(...). A list as delayed_window_ps, or records that is not an object, raised TypeError or AttributeError, which python -m minidaq_analysis does not catch: the tool ended with a traceback instead of 'error: ...' and status 2.

evaluation.rationale: The tool writes no report when it stops, so no wrong QC result can be used; only a file changed after the run reaches it.

resolution.change: fill checks that scanner and records are objects and that the crystal counts and the delayed window are integers, and raises FormatError otherwise, which the tool reports with status 2.
resolution.verification: test_report.py::test_metadata_with_a_field_of_another_type_is_an_error_not_a_crash writes runs whose window is a list, a string, null and a boolean: it failed before the change (checked) and passes after it.

whys: fill read the fields with subscripts and int(), which raise TypeError or AttributeError for another type, and the tool catches only the errors a reader of a valid file raises.
The metadata is written by MiniDAQ's own sink, so its reader was written for the files the sink makes.
root_cause.cause: Files written by MiniDAQ's own programs were not counted as external input (CAPA-0005).
root_cause.escape: No test changed a field's type in the metadata.

reports.title: The plan does not say when a failed check of the release checks may run again
reports.found: 2026-11-16, independent review of release 2.0.0 (the gate's first verdict on BM_HistogramRecord)
reports.description: Part 3 of the release checks of 2.0.0 failed on the regression gate (BM_HistogramRecord at 0.917 of 1.3.0, p = 0.0057), was investigated (identical machine code but for addresses, no source changed, alternate runs by hand within the same range), and was run again in full; the second result passed and is the one recorded, with the first kept in perf-ab-first/. The investigation was sound, but SDP section 8 has no rule for it: nothing limits how often a failed check may run again or what must be shown before, so a check could be repeated until it passes. tools/release_checks.sh's resume runs a failed part again by design.

evaluation.rationale: A rule of the release process. The one case so far was investigated before the rerun and both results are in the evidence; a gate that measures a 2 ns benchmark against an unchanged machine code cannot hide a defect of the product.

resolution.change: SDP version 20 (draft, approved with the next release's documents) adds the rule to section 8: investigate first; run again only when the cause is not in the commit (for the gate, the benchmark's machine code compared) or is of the machine or the tool with its own report; keep both results in the record; at most once per release, and a second failure is a problem report against the commit. tools/release_checks.sh resume enforces it (release 2.0.1): a failed part runs again only when OUT/rerun-part-N.md holds its investigation, and never a third time (status 4).
resolution.verification: The 2.0.0 record's handling of BM_HistogramRecord meets the rule (investigation before the rerun, both results kept), so no release is affected in its outcome. tools.release_checks: ReleaseChecks.test_a_failed_part_runs_again_only_after_its_investigation and test_a_part_that_failed_twice_does_not_run_a_third_time.

whys: tools/release_checks.sh resume was added (Theme D) to continue a run that stopped, and runs a failed part again by design.
The plan's section 8 asks that every check pass, and says nothing of a check that failed once.
root_cause.cause: A tool gained a way to repeat a check before the plan said when that is allowed.
root_cause.escape: The first release that used it was 2.0.0; its record explained the rerun, and no review compared that with the plan.

reports.title: CAPA-0005's fuzz target leaves out the reader of MDQ-PR-075, so rule 3.4 is not met
reports.found: 2026-11-16, independent review of release 2.0.0 (CAPA-0005 against coding standard rule 3.4)
reports.description: Coding standard version 9, rule 3.4, says that a reader of a JSON file joins fuzz_documents as a mode of its own. fuzz_documents has five modes; the reader of a list-mode file's delayed window, fixed for MDQ-PR-075, is not one of them, because it was written inside minidaq_listmode's main, where no fuzz target can call it. CAPA-0005's investigation table says 'none for the field' and its corrective action does not name the exception.

evaluation.rationale: The reader is checked since MDQ-PR-075 and tools.listmode tests a field of another type; the gap is that no fuzzer keeps it checked.

resolution.change: The read moved into the library: control::metadata_delayed_window_ps (listmode_sink.hpp), which minidaq_listmode sino calls. fuzz_documents gains mode 5 for it, with the seeds metadata and metadata-mdq-pr-075; fuzz/README.md lists it.
resolution.verification: ListModeSink.ReadsTheDelayedWindowFromMetadataAsUntrustedInput (ten inputs of other types and one good one) and tools.listmode pass; the fuzz build compiles the new mode and runs its seeds.

whys: The fix of MDQ-PR-075 kept the read where it was, in the tool's main.
The CAPA's corrective action listed the modes that existed, not the readers of its own investigation table.
root_cause.cause: The corrective action was checked against its list of modes, not against the rule it wrote.
root_cause.escape: The internal audit and the release checks ran fuzz_documents; nothing compares its modes with the readers the CAPA lists.

reports.title: SRS-CTL-022's test does not send a 2.x request or check that the refusal names the migration note
reports.found: 2026-11-16, independent review of release 2.0.0 (the coverage review's added test)
reports.description: SRS-CTL-022 (changed by CR-0030) asks that a request of another major version be refused naming the migration note. ControlProtocol.VersioningAndMalformedInput sends 4.0, 1.1, a number and, since the coverage review, no version, but no 2.x request, the clients that CR-0030 breaks, and checks only the error code, not the message.

evaluation.rationale: The server does what the requirement asks (the message is built from api_migration_hint for every refusal of a version); only its verification was incomplete.

resolution.change: The test sends {"api":"2.1"} and checks the code unsupported_api and that the message contains docs/migration-2.0.md.
resolution.verification: ControlProtocol.VersioningAndMalformedInput passes on the debug build.

whys: The coverage review added the case whose branch was untaken, a request without a version.
A 2.x version takes the same branch as 1.1 and 4.0, so coverage could not show it missing.
root_cause.cause: A requirement's clauses were checked against branch coverage, not read one by one against the test.
root_cause.escape: Branch coverage was complete for the line; the requirement's clause about the message had no assertion.

reports.title: The download page offers main's development build after a release, not the released edition
reports.found: 2026-11-16, independent review of release 2.0.0 (pages run 231 on cb30b81, VERSION 2.0.1-dev)
reports.description: pages.yml builds the book from every push to main. Right after a release tools/post_release.py sets VERSION to the next -dev version, so the download page and the web edition show 'Version 2.0.1-dev' and offer detector-to-diagnosis-v2.0.1-dev.pdf, which is not the released 2.0.0 that the record, the archive and the printed edition hold. Between releases the page also shows unreleased chapters and changes.

evaluation.rationale: The book, not the product; the dev build carries its version in every file name.

resolution.change: pages.yml builds from the last book-v tag of .github/tags.txt, with main's book/errata.json; until that tag exists it builds main as before, and the end of the tags workflow triggers it again.
resolution.verification: To be seen on the first run after the merge: the run's log names the tag, and the page says Version 2.0.0 (the session cannot reach github.io).

whys: The page was made when every push was a step toward the next release.
The post-release bump (Theme D) came later and nobody looked at the page after it.
root_cause.cause: The publication of the book had no rule for which version it serves.
root_cause.escape: Release checks end at the tag; nothing checks the public page after the post-release commit.

reports.title: The release record's skeleton names the hardened preset as the shipped binaries, not the product preset
reports.found: 2026-11-17, independent review of release 2.0.1 (docs/regulatory/releases/2.0.1.md, section Build)
reports.description: tools/release_record.py writes a record's Build section with 'cmake --preset hardened ... # the shipped binaries' and without 'ci/run_all.sh product'. Since CR-0029 (2.0.0) the shipped programs are the product preset's, which the release checks build and tools/repro_check.sh compares. The 2.0.0 record was corrected by hand; the 2.0.1 record, written from the skeleton, kept the old lines, so it tells a reader to build the wrong binaries from the tag.

evaluation.rationale: A record's instructions, not the product; the released binaries and their reproducibility evidence are the product preset's.

resolution.change: The skeleton names ci/run_all.sh product and the product preset as the shipped binaries; the 2.0.1 record's Build section is corrected, with a note that says so.
resolution.verification: tools.release_record passes; docs tests pass on the corrected 2.0.1 record.

whys: CR-0029 changed what ships; the 2.0.0 record was edited by hand, the tool that writes records was not.
Nothing compares a record's Build section with the presets.
root_cause.cause: A change of what ships updated one record, not its generator.
root_cause.escape: The record check reads the evidence paths and sections, not the commands.

reports.title: After a failed whole run, release_checks.sh resume blames every part for the failure
reports.found: 2026-11-17, independent review of release 2.0.1 (tools/release_checks.sh, the rule of MDQ-PR-077)
reports.description: A whole run (PART all) ends with one line, 'N release checks failed (part all)', and resume counted that line as a failure of each of the four parts. After a whole run in which only part 3 failed, resume refused to go on until rerun-part-1.md held an investigation of part 1, which had passed, then ran parts 1 and 2 again; and a later failure of any part counted as its second, so resume refused a run that SDP section 8 allows.

evaluation.rationale: The release process, not the product; the defect refuses runs, it never lets a failed check through.

resolution.change: A whole run also writes each part's verdict ('all release checks passed (part N)' or 'K release checks failed (part N)'), and resume counts only a part's own verdicts.
resolution.verification: tools.release_checks: test_a_whole_run_records_each_parts_verdict and test_resume_after_a_failed_whole_run_asks_only_for_the_failed_part.

whys: MDQ-PR-077's rule was enforced on the lines resume already read, and a whole run had no line per part.
The tests covered runs part by part, the way releases since 1.2.0 have run.
root_cause.cause: The whole run's summary did not say which part failed.
root_cause.escape: No test of resume after a whole run that failed.

reports.title: The codebase survey restarts a file's history at a rename
reports.found: 2026-11-17, writing Exercise 34.4 (tools/survey.py, churn)
reports.description: churn() counted a renamed file under its new name only in the commit that made the rename; the commits before it counted under the old name, which is no longer a file and drops out of the survey. A source file renamed after ten commits would have ranked with one. No file under minidaq/ has been renamed, so no survey the book reports was affected.

evaluation.rationale: A T1 tool whose output informs where to read first; it is neither in the product nor verification evidence, and no reported survey contained a rename.

resolution.change: churn() reads the log newest first and keeps a map from old names to the current one, so the commits made under every earlier name count for the file as it is called now; renamed() returns both sides of a rename.
resolution.verification: tools.survey: test_the_commits_before_a_rename_count_under_the_new_name (a file renamed twice, four commits).

whys: The rename was handled per numstat line, and a line knows only its own commit.
The test of renames had the rename and a later commit, never an earlier one.
root_cause.cause: A rename relates commits on both sides of it, and the parser looked at one line at a time.
root_cause.escape: No test with a commit made before a rename.

reports.title: A UID, a code string or an update's version with a trailing newline passes validation
reports.found: 2026-11-17, writing Exercise 35.4 (tools/dicom/uid.py, valid)
reports.description: Four validations matched a pattern anchored with ^ and $ through re.match, and Python's $ also matches just before a final newline. uid.valid('1.2.3\n') was true, so the export accepted an order whose study UID ended in a newline (SRS-DCM-005 and RC-47 say it refuses an invalid one); the encoder's last check accepted a UI or CS value ending in a newline; and make_update.py accepted --version '0.5.1\n' (since 0.5.0). No order or release used such a value.

evaluation.rationale: RC-47 (H-15) was weaker than specified: a study UID that is not the order's by one character could have reached the archive, which would file the series under a study that is not the order's. It needs a newline at the end of the hospital's UID, which no test order or worklist has given; the patient attributes were not affected.

resolution.change: The four checks use fullmatch: uid.valid, the encoder's CS and UI checks, and make_update.py's version.
resolution.verification: tools.dicom: test_an_order_that_cannot_file_the_series_is_refused and test_a_value_that_breaks_its_vr_is_refused_not_truncated with a trailing newline; tools.make_update: test_a_version_with_a_trailing_newline_is_refused. All three fail without the change.

whys: re.match with ^...$ reads as 'the whole string' and is not: $ matches before a final newline.
The tests of invalid values had wrong characters, empty values and leading zeros, never a trailing newline.
root_cause.cause: A validation pattern anchored with $ instead of matched with fullmatch.
root_cause.escape: No test with whitespace at the end of a value.

reports.title: The CI failed on main for six days, unnoticed, while commits were pushed
reports.found: 2026-11-23, internal audit before release 2.1.0 (the CI runs of main since 2026-11-17)
reports.description: Every CI run on main from 9a92709 (2026-11-17, Exercise 29.4) to 13bfdb3 (2026-11-22), about 30 commits, failed: tests.waits found an untagged thread start, sleep and clock reads in Exercise 29.4's test, which seven build-test jobs run, and from 2026-11-18 the vulnerability-scan job found eight new libssl3t64 CVEs without a triage decision. Each commit was pushed after a subset of the tests (ctest -R with the tests of the change) passed locally, and no one read the CI's result before the next push. No release was made from a red commit.

evaluation.rationale: The test's tags and the triage decisions are process evidence; no product code was wrong, and the eight CVEs are in OpenSSL features MiniDAQ does not use (SOUP list review of 2026-11-23). A release would have been stopped by SDP section 8, which tags only a green commit.

resolution.change: 6162e1e tags the test's waits and adds the eight triage decisions. CAPA-0006: SDP version 22 asks for the whole unit suite (ctest -L unit) before pushing a change to a test or a tool, and for the CI result of the last pushed commit to be read before the next push or within the day, a red result getting a problem report the same day.
resolution.verification: tests.waits and the ch29/e4 tests pass locally; the CI run on 6162e1e (vulnerability-scan and the build-test jobs).

whys: Two checks that run only in CI, or only in the full suite, failed and nothing reported it to the developer.
The developer ran only the tests named for each change and pushed without reading the CI result of the previous push.
The SDP says when CI must be green (before a tag) but not when its result must be read.
root_cause.cause: No rule said when a pushed commit's CI result is read, and the local check before a push was a subset of the suite.
root_cause.escape: SDP section 8 checks CI only at the release commit; the audit before the release is where it was found.

reports.title: Exercise 29.4's test of the GIL fails when the other thread gets no CPU during the call
reports.found: 2026-11-23, CI run 364 on fbe436b, job build-test (debug): ch29/e4_in_place/solution/unittest
reports.description: test_python_threads_run_during_the_call counts how often a second Python thread notes the time during the first half of one 3e7-element call of the solution, and requires more than 10. On the loaded CI runner (ctest in parallel, debug build) the second thread got no CPU during that half once and the test saw 0, although the solution releases the GIL. Found under CAPA-0006's rule, on the first CI run read after a push.

evaluation.rationale: An exercise's test, not MiniDAQ; the defect made a correct solution fail, never let a wrong one pass.

resolution.change: The test makes up to five calls and passes as soon as one shows the other thread running; a starter that holds the GIL sees 0 in all five, so it still fails.
resolution.verification: ch29/e4_in_place/solution/unittest passes in debug 5 times in a row and in release; the starter fails it with [0, 0, 0, 0, 0].

whys: One call gave the other thread one chance to be scheduled, and a busy machine can withhold it for 50 ms.
The test was written and run on an idle machine, where the thread always ran.
root_cause.cause: A test of scheduling that made one observation where the scheduler gives no guarantee for one.
root_cause.escape: The solution's test ran alone, never under ctest -j on a loaded machine, before it was pushed; CAPA-0001's rule for timing tests (a margin and a reason) was not applied to a test of threads.

reports.title: The release record's skeleton names the soak as 30 minutes after CR-0035 made it 100
reports.found: 2026-11-23, writing the release record of 2.1.0 from tools/release_record.py skeleton
reports.description: CR-0035 changed the release checks' soak to 100 minutes (tools/release_checks.sh, acceptance.json ACC-03), but the skeleton's row for it kept the label "soak, 30 minutes". A record written from the skeleton would have stated the wrong length next to evidence of 100 minutes.

evaluation.rationale: A label in a tool that drafts a record; the checks and the acceptance verdict measure 100 minutes, and a person reads each row before the record is checked.

resolution.change: The skeleton's row is "soak, 100 minutes", and a new test, test_the_soak_row_names_the_length_the_release_checks_run, reads the length from release_checks.sh and requires the row to name it.
resolution.verification: tools/test_release_record.py passes, and the new test fails with the label of 30 minutes; the skeleton of 2.1.0 has the row "soak, 100 minutes".

whys: The label was a string in the skeleton's table of checks, not read from release_checks.sh or acceptance.json.
CR-0035's impact analysis listed the script, the acceptance specification, the SRS, the SDP and the test plan, but not the record's skeleton.
root_cause.cause: A duration written twice, in the checks and in the tool that drafts their record, changed in one place only.
root_cause.escape: The skeleton's test checked the label it had, not the length the checks run.

reports.title: The C++ projector refuses a float64 output array whose dtype object is not NumPy's own
reports.found: 2026-11-23, independent review of release 2.1.0 (recon/python/recon_cpp.cpp, writable_out)
reports.description: CR-0034's check of an output array compared its dtype with float64 by identity (dtype().is), not by equivalence. NumPy shares one dtype object among most float64 arrays, but an array that was unpickled (multiprocessing, joblib, np.load of a pickle) or built through newbyteorder() twice has a float64 dtype object of its own, and forward(..., out=) and back(..., out=) refused it with 'out must be float64, got float64'. SRS-REC-009 refuses only an output that is not float64. Exercise 29.4's solution and its hint teach the same check.

evaluation.rationale: The defect refuses a valid output with an error and writes nothing; it never accepts an output it cannot write, so no projection is lost or wrong (RC-43 holds). A big-endian float64, which the C++ cannot write, is still refused.

resolution.change: writable_out() and the exercise's writable_float64() accept an output that py::isinstance<py::array_t<double>> accepts: a NumPy array whose dtype is equivalent to float64 in native byte order (PyArray_EquivTypes). The exercise's hint names that check.
resolution.verification: tools.recon_cpp: test_writes_into_an_output_the_caller_gives with an unpickled array, and test_refuses_an_output_it_cannot_write_in_place with a big-endian one; ch29/e4_in_place/solution: test_a_float64_output_with_a_dtype_object_of_its_own_is_written. The unpickled case fails without the change ('out must be float64, got float64').

whys: The dtype was compared with dtype().is(), which pybind11 inherits from py::object: the identity of two Python objects.
The tests' outputs were all made by np.zeros or np.empty, which use NumPy's shared float64 object, so identity and equality never differed in them.
root_cause.cause: A type check by object identity where the type system defines equivalence.
root_cause.escape: No test gave an output made another way than np.zeros or np.empty; the refusal tests checked that wrong outputs are refused, not that every right one is accepted.

reports.title: The release record of 2.1.0 names a soak of 30 minutes next to evidence of 100
reports.found: 2026-11-23, independent review of release 2.1.0 (docs/regulatory/releases/2.1.0.md, table of checks)
reports.description: The table of checks in the 2.1.0 record has the row 'soak, 30 minutes', although soak.txt reports 100 minutes and the record's own notes say 100. MDQ-PR-087 corrected the skeleton's row while the record was written, and its verification read a new skeleton, not the record; the record's table was not written again from it. tools/release_record.py check compares a record's evidence paths and results with the rules of Exercise 14.5, not its rows with what the evidence gives, so the record passed. It is the third report in two releases of a record stating what its evidence does not (MDQ-PR-081, MDQ-PR-087).

evaluation.rationale: A label in a record; the soak, the acceptance verdict (ACC-03, 100 minutes) and the evidence are right.

resolution.change: The record's row says 100 minutes, with a note that the review corrected it. tools/release_record.py check now writes the table's rows from the record's evidence (table_rows, the skeleton's own function) and refuses a record that lacks one of them as written (table_drift).
resolution.verification: tools.release_record: test_a_table_row_that_differs_from_the_evidence_is_refused (a stale soak label and a changed result are refused) and test_the_newest_record_has_every_row_its_evidence_gives, which fails on the record as released.

whys: The record's table was copied from a skeleton written before MDQ-PR-087's fix, and nothing compared it with the evidence again.
The record check verifies that the evidence paths exist and the results pass, not that the rows are the ones the evidence gives.
root_cause.cause: The record check did not compare the record's table with the table its evidence gives.
root_cause.escape: MDQ-PR-087's verification checked the skeleton, not the record written from it; the internal audit's O-8 judged the repeated cause closed by the skeleton's test.

reports.title: The record check judges old records by today's table and fails every record before 2.1.0
reports.found: 2026-11-23, merging the review of release 2.1.0 (PR #21): release_record.py check on docs/regulatory/releases/2.0.1.md
reports.description: MDQ-PR-089 made release_record.py check compare a record's table with the rows the skeleton writes from the evidence. The rows are today's: the soak row says 100 minutes, and the product preset's row exists. Every record before 2.1.0 then failed: 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 on the soak's length (their soaks lasted 30 minutes and their tables say so), the earlier ones on rows that did not exist when they were written. No test ran the check on old records, so CI stayed green.

evaluation.rationale: A check of records, run by hand before a tag; it refused correct records and accepted no wrong one.

resolution.change: The soak row's label takes the length that the release's own soak check names in release-checks.txt (soak_label), and the comparison applies from 2.0.0 on (FIRST_TABLE), the first record with every row of today's table.
resolution.verification: tools/test_release_record.py: test_every_record_since_the_table_took_its_form_matches_its_evidence (2.0.0, 2.0.1 and 2.1.0 pass) and test_the_soak_row_takes_the_length_of_the_release_it_records; both fail before the change.

whys: The check took the labels of the table from a constant that describes the present release checks.
The fix was tested on the newest record and on a made-up one, not on the records already in the repository.
root_cause.cause: A check of historical records written against the present rules, not the rules each record was made under.
root_cause.escape: The new check was run on the newest record only; a run over every record would have shown it.

reports.title: CI fails on the commit that lists a release's tag, because VERSION is still the release
reports.found: 2026-11-23, CI run 367 on ee34473 (Tag book-v2.1.0 on the release commit), docs.version in every build-test job; read under CAPA-0006 while starting 2.2.0
reports.description: The release is tagged through .github/tags.txt in a commit after the release commit, and the -dev bump comes after that. On the tag-list commit VERSION is still X.Y.Z, and tools/check_version.py accepts X.Y.Z only in a commit whose subject starts "Release X.Y.Z", so docs.version failed in all seven build-test jobs. The next commit, ec2182e (2.1.1-dev), was green. The failure was found about an hour after the push, when the CI runs of the morning were read, not right after the push as CAPA-0006 asks.

evaluation.rationale: A rule about the version string of a commit that changes only the tag list; no program differs from the release commit's.

resolution.change: check_version.py also accepts X.Y.Z in the commit whose subject starts "Tag book-vX.Y.Z ", the commit that lists the release's tag; any other commit with a release version still fails.
resolution.verification: tools/test_check_version.py: the tag-list commit of the same version passes, one naming another version fails; docs.version passes.

whys: The version rule (MDQ-PR-024) was written before tags were made by a workflow from .github/tags.txt, which needs a commit of its own after the release commit.
The order release, tag list, -dev bump was followed at each release, and the red run on the tag-list commit was replaced by a green one a few minutes later.
root_cause.cause: A rule about release commits that did not know the release procedure's second commit.
root_cause.escape: The CI result of the tag-list commit was not read before the next push: the -dev bump was pushed eleven minutes later, while that run was still going, against SDP version 22, section 5.

reports.title: The 2.2.0 roadmap was pushed without its place in the design file, and docs.design_file fails
reports.found: 2026-11-23, ctest -L unit before the next push, after c98f417 (Roadmap 2.2.0) was on main
reports.description: docs/ROADMAP-2.2.0.md is a planning document, and tools/design_file.py requires every roadmap to be in a clause of the design file (7.3.2). The unit suite was run before the file was added to git, and the check lists files with git ls-files, so it did not see the new file and passed; CI on c98f417 sees it and fails.

evaluation.rationale: An index of documents; the roadmap's content was right and reviewed.

resolution.change: The roadmap is listed under clause 7.3.2 of design-file.json, and design-file.md is written again from it.
resolution.verification: docs.design_file passes with the roadmap tracked.

whys: The suite ran on a working tree whose new file was not yet staged, and the check reads tracked files only.
SDP section 5 asks for the whole unit suite before a push, but not on the tree as it will be committed.
root_cause.cause: The check before a push ran on a tree that differed from the commit pushed.
root_cause.escape: The new file was staged after the suite ran; nothing ran the suite on the commit itself before the push.

reports.title: tools.agent_gate fails on CI, where clang-format is installed and git-clang-format is not
reports.found: 2026-11-23, the CI result of 6fe8a40 (Theme P1), read before the next push (CAPA-0006)
reports.description: The test of the agent gate skipped the known-bad change of the format check when clang-format was not on the path. The format check (tools/check_format.py) needs git-clang-format too, and is skipped without it. The build-test jobs install clang-format but not git-clang-format on the path, so the gate skipped the check, gave PASS for the unformatted change, and the test, which had not skipped, failed in every build-test job of ci on main.

evaluation.rationale: A test of a development tool; the gate reported the format check as skipped, as it should, and the programs did not change.

resolution.change: The test skips a known-bad change when the gate itself reports that change's check as skipped, instead of guessing from the path which tools the check needs.
resolution.verification: tools.agent_gate passes with clang-format and git-clang-format, and skips case 09 with neither (a run with a path that holds only python3 and git).

whys: The test decided by itself whether the format check could run, from one of the two programs the check needs.
The machine the test was written on has both programs, as does the format job of CI; the build-test jobs have one.
root_cause.cause: A test that duplicated, incompletely, the condition under which the tool it tests skips a check.
root_cause.escape: The suite ran only where both programs are installed; no local run had clang-format without git-clang-format.

reports.title: Static analysis fails on main after Theme S: an unused return value in the node merge
reports.found: 2026-11-23, the CI result of ac7f3bc (Theme S), read before the next push (CAPA-0006)
reports.description: NodeMerge::end checked its node's index with (void)offsets_.at(node). clang-tidy's bugprone-unused-return-value, an error in the static-analysis job, refuses a discarded at(); the gate's self-test, which runs the same analysis on the correct tree, failed with it. cppcheck, run afterwards on the same tree, also asked for a vector parameter of a helper to be passed by reference. The unit tests and the gate's fast checks passed, and neither runs static analysis.

evaluation.rationale: The code behaved as specified: the discarded at() threw for an unknown node, as intended, and every other path was unchanged. The finding is the analysis's rule, not a fault in the merge; the node merge is used only with the simulator in 2.2.

resolution.change: NodeMerge::end throws std::out_of_range for an unknown node explicitly, and the constructor moves its offsets and leaves the refusal of zero nodes to the StreamMerger, without the helper that copied them.
resolution.verification: tools/static_analysis.sh's clang-tidy and cppcheck are clean on the changed sources; ctest -L unit passes; the node merge's tests, which refuse zero nodes, pass.

whys: Theme S was pushed after the unit suite and the gate's fast checks, which do not run static analysis; the gate's --full, which does, was not run.
CAPA-0006's rule before a push names the unit suite only, and a change of C++ code needs the analysis too.
root_cause.cause: A push of new C++ code without the static analysis that CI applies to it.
root_cause.escape: Static analysis runs only in CI and in the gate's --full mode; the local check before the push did not include it.

reports.title: Exercise 29.4's test of the GIL fails again on CI after five calls without the other thread running
reports.found: 2026-11-24, the CI result of ddc8d5a, job build-test (debug): ch29/e4_in_place/solution/unittest, read before the next push (CAPA-0006)
reports.description: test_python_threads_run_during_the_call failed in the debug build-test job on a commit that changed only HANDOFF.md, as MDQ-PR-086 did before its fix: five calls of the solution, each a chance for the second thread to be scheduled, all passed without it running on the loaded runner. The test passes locally, alone and repeated 20 times.

evaluation.rationale: An exercise's test, not MiniDAQ; the defect made a correct solution fail, never let a wrong one pass.

resolution.change: The test tries the call for up to 20 s instead of five times, and passes as soon as one call shows the other thread running; the failure message names the attempts.
resolution.verification: ch29/e4_in_place/solution/unittest passes in debug; the solution with its GIL release removed fails it after 22 attempts over 20 s, all with 0 stamps; tests.waits passes with the deadline's clock reads tagged.

whys: MDQ-PR-086's fix gave the scheduler five chances, a number chosen without a measure of how long a loaded runner can withhold a CPU.
A debug call takes about a second there, so five calls covered a few seconds of a runner running several test processes at once.
root_cause.cause: A margin of attempts with no basis in time, for a test of scheduling.
root_cause.escape: The fix of MDQ-PR-086 was verified by five runs in a row on an idle machine, not on a machine loaded as CI's is.

reports.title: The release soak of 2.2.0 has 8 of 600 intervals above 10 ms, more than ACC-04 allows, each with a thread kept from a CPU
reports.found: 2026-11-24, release checks of 2.2.0, part 3, on 5647d2e: tools/acceptance.py judged ACC-04 FAIL (592 of 600 intervals within 10 ms, 98.7%)
reports.description: Every check of part 3 passed, but 8 of the soak's 600 intervals of 10 s had a 99th percentile above 10 ms (up to 62.65 ms), where ACC-04 allows six (CR-0035). In each, one server thread waited 21 to 61 ms in one second for a CPU while runnable (mdq-write, mdq-decode or mdq-sort); steal over the intervals averaged 0.66% (0.25% in 2.1.0's soak), per second up to 6.79%. The pipeline ran at about 4% of its capacity, and the single-node source of CR-0037 runs the same generator statements; the regression gate against book-v2.1.0 passed. The symptom is MDQ-PR-064's.

evaluation.rationale: No single was lost or arrived after the sorter's window (the soak counts no loss and the run is complete); the latency is not a risk control of a hazard, as for MDQ-PR-064.

reports.decision: Run part 3 of the release checks again once, in full, on the same commit (SDP section 8; investigation in the release's rerun-part-3.md). A second failure of ACC-04 is a problem report against the commit and stops the release for the software lead. Part 3 ran again the same day: ACC-04 failed again, 11 of 600 intervals (highest 20.45 ms, each again with one thread waiting 21 to 77 ms for a CPU, steal mean 0.83%), and the regression gate judged BM_SortFunctor slower (0.862, p 0.0026), a benchmark it had passed in the first run, of a sorter whose source did not change since 2.1.0. The release stops for the software lead. Control the same evening: book-v2.1.0's programs, built anew, had 6 of 600 intervals above 10 ms on the same machine (3 at their release), with the same CPU waits; the candidate's 19 of 1,200 is 1.6 times that rate, not distinguishable from chance in two soaks. BM_SortFunctor's machine code is the same in both builds (measurements/mdq-pr-096/). Decided on 2026-11-24 by the software lead (the coordinator under the author's standing delegation of 2026-11-15, 2026-11-23 and 2026-11-24, in writing in the project): release 2.2.0 with a recorded deviation for ACC-04 and for the regression gate's verdict on BM_SortFunctor, as for MDQ-PR-064 at 1.0.0, on the control soak (the 2.1.0 programs at the limit on the same machine) and the benchmark's unchanged machine code. The report stays open; CR-0038 proposes for 2.3.0 that the latency be judged against the previous release's programs, interleaved on the same machine. Review of 2.2.0 (MDQ-PR-099): a CPU wait of 20 ms or more is in 99% of all intervals of the three soaks, so its presence in the slow ones is no evidence for the machine; the control soak is (p = 0.22). The candidate's 19 of 1,200 does not show SRS-PERF-022 met (p = 0.037 against 1%): 'affects' names 2.2.0, which was released with the anomaly.

reports.title: The test of the newest release record fails as soon as a problem report is opened after the release
reports.found: 2026-11-24, ctest -L unit before pushing MDQ-PR-096 (CAPA-0006): tools.release_record failed with 'open report MDQ-PR-096 is not listed' in the record of 2.1.0
reports.description: test_the_newest_record_passes_the_rules_of_its_release judged the record of the last release with the rules of its commit but against today's problem reports, so a report opened between releases made the record look incomplete. Until now every report opened after a release was closed before the next push, so the test never met an open one.

evaluation.rationale: A test of the project's tools; it refused a correct record, it never accepted a wrong one.

resolution.change: The test reads the files of the commit that last wrote the record (git archive of docs and measurements) and judges the record against them; a record not yet committed is judged against the working tree.
resolution.verification: tools.release_record passes with MDQ-PR-096 open; the earlier test fails on the same tree.

whys: The test took the rules from the record's commit but the files from the working tree.
The two had only differed by closed reports, which the check does not ask a record to list.
root_cause.cause: A test that judged a past record by present data.
root_cause.escape: No report had stayed open across a push since the test was written.

reports.title: The release record check has no way to accept a check released with the software lead's deviation
reports.found: 2026-11-24, writing the record of 2.2.0: tools/release_record.py check refused the rows of ACC-04 and the regression gate, which the software lead had released with a deviation
reports.description: SDP section 8 lets the software lead release with a failed check, recorded with the decision (1.0.0 did so for ACC-04). Since Theme R the check of a record compares each table row with the evidence and requires the performance row to pass, so a record that states the deviation honestly cannot pass it, and one that passes it would misstate the evidence.

evaluation.rationale: A tool of the release records; it refused a correct record, it never accepted a wrong one.

resolution.change: A row may say 'fail (deviation)' where the evidence gives FAIL or pass, when the record has a non-empty section Deviation; the check then excuses only the exercise check's 'is not pass' error of that row. Exercise 14.5's own check is unchanged.
resolution.verification: tools.release_record: test_a_failed_check_passes_only_as_a_recorded_deviation (refused without the section or with an empty one, accepted with it, no other error excused); the 2.2.0 record passes the check.

whys: Theme R made the table follow the evidence row by row.
No release since 1.0.0 had failed a check, so the path of SDP section 8 for a deviation was not exercised by the new check.
root_cause.cause: A check written for the passing case only.
root_cause.escape: The skeleton's tests covered a stale row and a failed row, not a failed row that was released.

reports.title: The deviation of release 2.2.0 rests on a plan without a deviation path, on CPU waits found in nearly every interval, and on a record check that excuses rows the decision does not name
reports.found: 2026-11-24, independent review of release 2.2.0 (measurements/review-2.2.0/)
reports.description: Three faults of the record, not of the decision. (1) SDP version 23, section 8, releases only when every check passes and every acceptance criterion is PASS; it has no deviation, although MDQ-PR-098 and the record say section 8 allows one (1.0.0 used one too). (2) The record, MDQ-PR-096 and CR-0038 give, as evidence for the machine, a server thread waiting 20 to 77 ms for a CPU in every slow interval; such a wait is in 594, 598 and 594 of the 600 intervals of the three soaks, slow or not. The record also does not say that the candidate's 19 of 1,200 slow intervals do not show SRS-PERF-022 met (p = 0.037 against 1%). (3) tools/release_record.py check excused every row marked 'fail (deviation)' once the record had any non-empty section Deviation, whether or not the section named that check. The gate's verdict on BM_SortFunctor was compared on the benchmark's own body only, without the sort it calls or its input.

evaluation.rationale: Records and a tool of the release process; the corrected evidence supports the same decision (no evidence that 2.2.0 is worse than 2.1.0: control p = 0.22; the sort, its callee and its input identical in both builds), and the latency is no risk control.

resolution.change: The 2.2.0 record's section Deviation names the rows it releases and has a note with the corrected reasons; MDQ-PR-096 and CR-0038 corrected; the check excuses a 'fail (deviation)' row only when the section Deviation names it as `row`; SDP version 24 (draft) adds the deviation to section 8 with what its record states; measurements/review-2.2.0/ holds the comparison of the sort with its callee and its input, and the table of waits.
resolution.verification: tools.release_record: test_a_failed_check_passes_only_as_a_recorded_deviation refuses a section that names another check (fails without the change); the 2.2.0 record passes the check.

whys: The deviation was written under time pressure after a second failure, from the evidence of MDQ-PR-064's method, which records the largest wait of each interval but not how common such a wait is.
The record check was extended for the one case at hand (MDQ-PR-098) and tested with one section Deviation that covered every row.
The plan's section 8 was not reread when the record cited it.
root_cause.cause: A deviation argued from a coincidence without its base rate, and a plan and a check that did not state what a deviation must show.
root_cause.escape: The release decision was made by one reviewer the same evening; the independent review after release is the check that found it.

reports.title: The agent's command hook allows a push that deletes main or forces with combined short options
reports.found: 2026-11-24, independent review of release 2.2.0, the hook run on chosen commands
reports.description: tools/hooks/agent_command.py refuses --delete, -d, --force, -f and a '+' refspec, but allowed 'git push origin :main' (a refspec with an empty source deletes the remote branch, and its destination 'main' is allowed) and 'git push -fu origin main' (the force among combined short options).

evaluation.rationale: A development tool; .claude/settings.json asks a person before every git push, so the hook is the second control, and no such push was made.

resolution.change: A refspec that starts with ':' is refused as a delete; an argument of two or more short options is refused when it holds f or d.
resolution.verification: tools.test_agent_hooks: test_a_delete_by_empty_source_or_a_force_among_short_options_is_refused (fails without the change); -u alone is still allowed.

whys: The hook matched whole arguments against a list of option spellings.
Its tests listed the spellings the hook knew.
root_cause.cause: A deny list of spellings instead of the meanings of git's refspec and option syntax.
root_cause.escape: No test tried the other spellings of the same operations.

reports.title: The acceptance report names the absolute path of the machine that ran the checks
reports.found: 2026-11-24, independent review of release 2.2.0: measurements/release-2.2.0/acceptance.md names the checkout's absolute path, against CLAUDE.md's privacy rule
reports.description: tools/acceptance.py wrote 'evidence from' with the OUT directory as given, an absolute path of the machine; the reports of 1.0.0 to 2.1.0 name scratch directories the same way, and that of 2.2.0 the checkout under a home directory. The repository is public.

evaluation.rationale: A report of the release process; the paths hold no personal data, but the rule forbids them.

resolution.change: The report names the directory relative to the repository when inside it, else 'OUT (name)'; the line of the 2.2.0 report is corrected. Earlier reports are kept as released.
resolution.verification: tools.test_acceptance: test_the_report_names_no_absolute_path_of_the_machine (fails without the change).

whys: The report printed its argument as given.
The agent file checker looks for absolute paths in agent files only.
root_cause.cause: A generated, committed report with no check of the privacy rule.
root_cause.escape: The privacy rule is checked on agent files, not on evidence.
